title: Firehall Double Smash Burgers BBQ
seoTitle: Firehall Double Smash Burgers BBQ | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Smash burger energy with BBQ sauce built for the hall line
subtitle: Double patties, BBQ sauce, and crispy onions for ten
description: Adapted from classic smash burger and BBQ hall traditions (BBQ Pit Boys, Hey Grill Hey): double 3-oz patties get smashed on a hot griddle, stacked with cheddar, BBQ sauce, and crispy onions for ten hungry firefighters.

steps.title: Portion smash balls
steps.instruction: Divide beef into 20 balls about 3 oz each. Keep cold until cooking. Mix ketchup, BBQ sauce, and Worcestershire for hall BBQ sauce.

steps.title: Crisp the onions
steps.instruction: Cook sliced onions in oil over medium-high until deep golden and crisp, about 12 minutes. Drain on paper towels.

steps.title: Smash first patties
steps.instruction: Heat griddle to medium-high. Place balls on surface, smash flat immediately with a stiff spatula. Season with salt and pepper. Cook 2 minutes until crust forms.

steps.title: Flip, cheese, stack
steps.instruction: Flip patties, add cheese, cook 1 minute. Stack double patties per bun bottom. Repeat in batches until all 10 doubles are built.

steps.title: Check doneness
steps.instruction: Thickest patty should hit 160°F internal. If needed, finish on cooler griddle zone without burning cheese.

steps.title: Toast buns
steps.instruction: Butter bun tops and toast on griddle 30 seconds until golden.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Wrap completed burgers in foil and hold at 170°F up to 10 minutes. Sauce and pickles added at the line.
Burgers wrapped in foil, crispy onions, BBQ sauce, pickles. Call it: double smash BBQ—grab and go.

proTips: Cold beef smashes cleaner—don't let balls warm on the counter.
Smash once hard; re-smashing pushes out juice.
Crispy onions go on at service or they steam soft in the wrap.
tonightSpread: Wrapped double smash burgers in a foil-lined pan.
Crispy onions, BBQ sauce, and pickles at the line.
leftovers: Chop patties into a BBQ burger hash with potatoes.
Crumble over loaded fries with extra sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Double smash is morale in handheld form. Cooks fast, holds wrapped 10 minutes, and beats plain grill night every time.
mealPrepNotes: Portion balls early and keep cold. Cook bacon and onions first. Wrap finished burgers in foil and hold at 170°F up to 10 minutes—toast buns last minute.
